title: Independent Windows WSL tmux terminal
sourceStatus: committed; not packaged, installed, or deployed

capabilities: Windows native Shell remains independent when WSL is unavailable
List installed WSL distributions and configure a selected distribution
Validate Linux absolute working directory and bind default Linux username plus UID
List, create, select, set default, attach, and reconnect to WSL tmux sessions
Reject changing the WSL target under an existing profile ID
boundaries: Independent WSL profile cannot bind to a managed project
No AI takeover, return, or host-process proof for WSL
Hub profile projection includes only runtime=wsl, not WSL username, UID, or cwd

regression.scope: New WSL adapter plus existing POSIX tmux, terminal manager, and Hub regressions

managerIntegration.scope: Fake WSL adapter and real local Mac PTY fixture

adapterIntermediateSummary.note: Overlapping/intermediate backend run; not added to the 53 distinct final regression and manager-integration cases.

historicalFailure.note: An earlier UID recheck failure was reproduced and retained as history; it is not the final result.

frontendBuild.note: Build emitted an existing lucide-react module-level use-client warning.

browserFixture.scope: Synthetic Windows-owner UI: native profile independent without WSL; distro selection; Windows path rejection and Linux path-with-spaces acceptance; no project binding; fixed runtime/distro on edit with cwd retained; no WSL Shell toggle or AI takeover; dark 390px layout without horizontal overflow.
browserFixture.limits: Synthetic owner UI only; not a real Windows account, WSL distribution, or physical phone.

delivery.currentlyInstalledMacUi: UI1066; does not include this WSL implementation
delivery.candidateBuild: BUILD1094 and Android v14 do not include this implementation
delivery.overallMilestone: M7 partial; platform-native validation and packaging remain open

limitations: No real Windows account, WSL distribution, tmux, or node-pty native acceptance was performed.
The passing tests use mocked WSL commands and local POSIX tmux/PTY fixtures.
Browser-fixture acceptance used a synthetic Windows-owner UI and does not substitute for native Windows/WSL/phone testing.
This report records evidence; it does not claim the full product or M7 is complete.
